question: Does lightonai/LightOnOCR-3-0.8B run locally on this Mac, free, no pod?
answer: yes, both backends; mlx-vlm is the usable one
venv: throwaway uv venv, Python 3.12: transformers 5.23.0, torch 2.15.0, mlx-vlm 0.7.12
input: page.png, 1240x1754, rendered by make_page.py (title, 3-line paragraph, 4x3 ruled table); truth in page_truth.json
mode: transcribe (empty prompt) only; grounding mode not tried

transformers_mps.note: CER on whitespace-normalised text with markdown/HTML markup stripped; first run includes weight download in load_s

mlx_vlm.note: CER on whitespace-normalised text with markdown/HTML markup stripped; first run includes weight download in load_s

summary: Both read the page exactly: CER 0.0 on 293 chars, 12/12 table cells, table as HTML. transformers on MPS took 481 s to generate 230 tokens (~2 s/token, unusable); mlx-vlm took 16.9 s for the same 230 tokens after a 23 s load from cache. transformers load_s includes the 1.7 GB first download.
caveat: one clean synthetic page, one run each, not timed warm; says nothing about hard pages
